type:
∀ (X : Finset Nat) (A B : Fin 2 → Finset ↥X),
  (∀ i, Finset.Nonempty (A i)) →
  (∀ j, Finset.Nonempty (B j)) →
  Pairwise (fun i i' => Disjoint (A i) (A i')) →
  Pairwise (fun j j' => Disjoint (B j) (B j')) →
  (∀ x : ↥X, ∃ i, x ∈ A i) →
  (∀ x : ↥X, ∃ j, x ∈ B j) →
  let n : Int := Int.ofNat (Finset.card X)
  let c : Int := Int.ofNat (Finset.card (A 0))
  let d : Int := Int.ofNat (Finset.card (B 0))
  ∀ R : Fin 2 → Fin 2 → Int,
    (∃ σ : Equiv.Perm ↥X, ∀ i j, R i j =
      Int.ofNat (Finset.card (A i ∩ Finset.map (Equiv.toEmbedding σ) (B j)))) ↔
    ∃! a : Int, max 0 (c + d - n) ≤ a ∧ a ≤ min c d ∧
      R 0 0 = a ∧ R 0 1 = c - a ∧ R 1 0 = d - a ∧ R 1 1 = n - c - d + a
sourceReason: Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, § 7.3, unnumbered two-block classification, p. 30. The published PDF matches the project copy. The supplied defect-report URL returned HTTP 404, and no correction for this endpoint was available. The two ordered partitions of X include singleton blocks when needed to cover X. By Proposition 7.3, the range over permutation representatives is the range of double-coset matrices. Their entries are cardinalities viewed as integers, and the upper-left entry determines the unique parameter. https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf
